name: Service and recall reminders
summary: Service and recall reminders: works out when each completed job's next service falls due, queues a reminder to the customer for approval, and records any text they send back. Crons read and queue; a person approves every message. Recall checks and bookings are not covered yet (see gaps).

fleet-account-reminders.evidence: 1 dealer service discovery call describes reminders and customer replies sent through a messaging tool, with bookings in the diary

covered_by.due-list-build: due-list (completed jobs past the service interval)
covered_by.customer-reply: replies (records inbound texts; the answer is a skill step)
covered_by.booking-diary: not built (a person books the visit in ServiceM8's diary)
covered_by.record-keeping: due records and replies in the workflow's store

crons.name: due-list
crons.summary: Once a day (21:00 UTC is 7 or 8 am in eastern Australia): completed jobs whose next service falls due in the window, with their contact.

crons.name: remind
crons.summary: Hourly: queue a service reminder for each due job, oldest due first, for a person to approve. Nothing is sent by the cron.

crons.name: replies
crons.summary: Record any text a customer sends back on a job whose reminder was approved and sent. Reads only.

draft_ops_note: Draft operations here are reads: completed jobs, their contacts, and inbound texts on a job. Nothing read leaves the business. Every reminder reaches a customer, so each one is a live operation and waits for a person.

servicem8.covers: completed jobs, job contacts and inbound texts (read); reminder SMS and email (approval only)

gaps: Service-due reminders by kilometres or by service schedule, recall checks and VIN lookups: not in the captured pages or the kit. This workflow uses one interval in months from the last completed job.
MechanicDesk and WorkshopMate: their help pages are captured, but the kit has no folder for either, so no operation is mapped. Their pages cover appointment reminders only.
Podium: the one call named it for reminders and replies. The kit maps its messaging operations, but no platform evidence was captured for it, so no adapter is built.
Vehicles are not separate records in ServiceM8's job fields, so a customer with two vehicles gets one reminder per completed job. The approver sees each job.
Booking the visit (booking-diary) and phone follow-up: not built. A person books in ServiceM8's diary.
Declined or deferred work and a due-date log: not built.
Customer replies by email: the replies cron reads SMS only. Answering a reply is a skill step, not a cron.

Marketing rule: ServiceM8's messaging docs say marketing and promotional SMS is not permitted. A service reminder is a service message, but confirm the customer consent wording with the client before the first live send.
Send window: ServiceM8's own booking reminders send SMS only between 7am and 7pm. The window for API sends is not confirmed, so approve reminders in business hours.
Docs-only until a ServiceM8 trial account proves the reminder sends, the job contact fields and the inbound SMS records.

evidence.calls: 1 automotive service discovery call, which described reminders and replies sent by a messaging tool and bookings in a diary
evidence.platforms: ServiceM8, MechanicDesk and WorkshopMate help pages on service reminders; only ServiceM8 has mapped operations in the kit
